# 🚗 MOVING DAY ESSENTIALS
### Ohio → Oregon | Keep This With the Car

---

## BEFORE YOU LEAVE — QUICK WALK-THROUGH
- [ ] Final walk-through video of every room, closet, and outdoor space
- [ ] All windows and doors locked
- [ ] All lights, fans, and appliances off
- [ ] Thermostat set or turned off
- [ ] Fridge emptied and unplugged
- [ ] Trash taken out
- [ ] Meter photos taken (gas, electric, water)
- [ ] Keys, fobs, and garage remotes returned — receipt in hand
- [ ] Bill of Lading signed and copy in your folder
- [ ] Nothing left in closets, cabinets, attic, garage, or storage unit

---

## DOCUMENTS FOLDER (rides in the car, not the truck)
- [ ] Driver's licenses / passports
- [ ] Vehicle titles, registrations, insurance cards
- [ ] Lease / closing papers (Ohio and Oregon)
- [ ] Moving contract, inventory list, Bill of Lading
- [ ] Vehicle shipping receipt and carrier contact
- [ ] Birth certificates, Social Security cards
- [ ] Medical records and current prescription list
- [ ] Insurance policy numbers (auto, renters/home, health)
- [ ] New landlord contact and move-in instructions
- [ ] Dog: rabies cert, vaccine records, microchip number, vet contact

---

## DOG BAG (accessible, not in the truck)
- [ ] Food and treats (3+ days' supply)
- [ ] Water and collapsible bowls
- [ ] Leash, harness, poop bags
- [ ] Current medications and dosing notes
- [ ] Favorite toy and familiar blanket
- [ ] Crate or car restraint set up and tested
- [ ] Calming aids if prescribed
- [ ] Vet records folder (duplicate of above)
- [ ] ID tag with current phone number

---

## PERSONAL ESSENTIALS BAG
- [ ] Cash ($200–$300 minimum for tips, tolls, emergencies)
- [ ] Credit and debit cards
- [ ] Phone chargers (car charger + cables for both phones)
- [ ] Portable battery pack, charged
- [ ] Laptop or tablet and charger if needed
- [ ] Medications (both people, full supply for the trip + 1 week buffer)
- [ ] Vitamins and any daily supplements
- [ ] Glasses, contacts, and solution
- [ ] Toiletries for 3–4 days (don't pack these in the truck)
- [ ] Change of clothes for 3–4 days (same)
- [ ] Snacks for the road (mixed nuts, bars, fruit, dog treats)
- [ ] Water bottles, filled
- [ ] Hand sanitizer and basic first aid kit

---

## CAR EMERGENCY KIT
- [ ] Jumper cables or jump starter pack
- [ ] Tire inflator / fix-a-flat
- [ ] Flashlight and extra batteries
- [ ] Reflective triangles or road flares
- [ ] Basic tool kit (screwdrivers, pliers, zip ties)
- [ ] Extra quart of oil and washer fluid
- [ ] Blanket (useful in mountain passes)
- [ ] Paper maps of the route (yes, really — dead zones exist)
- [ ] AAA card or roadside assistance number saved in phone

---

## CONTACTS — WRITTEN DOWN (don't rely only on your phone)

| Who | Name | Phone |
|---|---|---|
| Moving company | | |
| Mover day-of driver | | |
| Vehicle shipping carrier | | |
| New landlord / property mgr | | |
| Ohio landlord | | |
| Roadside assistance | | |
| Vet (Ohio) | | |
| Vet (Oregon / en route) | | |
| Emergency vet (destination) | | |

---

## MOVER TIPS — CASH, DAY OF
- [ ] Budget $20–$50 per mover as a tip for good service
- [ ] Keep cash separate and accessible
- [ ] Confirm payment method with the company before they arrive

---

Here's the full calendar. Each entry is formatted so you can copy the title line directly as an event name and drop the note in the event description field. Set them all as all-day events on the relevant date, with a morning alarm.

---

## HOW TO USE THIS
Figure out your move date, then count backward. I'll use **Week 0 = Move Day** so you can plug in your actual dates. Each reminder includes a suggested time of day for the alert.

---

## WEEK 8 (10 weeks out — do these now)

**Event:** Book movers or truck — get 3+ quotes
**Owner:** J | **Alert:** 8:00 AM
**Description:** Get binding estimates from 3 licensed interstate movers (verify USDOT on FMCSA). Also price U-Haul, Penske, PODS, and U-Pack. Decide by Week 7.

**Event:** Confirm Oregon housing — sign lease or set closing date
**Owner:** J | **Alert:** 8:00 AM
**Description:** If not yet signed, make this the top priority this week. Confirm dog-friendly. Get move-in date and landlord contact in writing.

**Event:** Book vet appointment — dog health check and records
**Owner:** M | **Alert:** 9:00 AM
**Description:** Get full vaccine records, rabies certificate, microchip number, and any travel meds. Ask about motion sickness or anxiety. Request a written copy of everything.

**Event:** Research Oregon DMV requirements
**Owner:** M | **Alert:** 10:00 AM
**Description:** Check Oregon DMV for new resident license and vehicle registration rules, emissions test requirements (Portland metro/Medford), and what documents you'll need to bring.

---

## WEEK 7

**Event:** Book movers or truck — decision deadline
**Owner:** J | **Alert:** 8:00 AM
**Description:** Choose your method (full-service, hybrid, or DIY) and book it today. Pay deposit only after verifying USDOT number and insurance. Get everything in writing.

**Event:** Book internet installation at Oregon address
**Owner:** J | **Alert:** 9:00 AM
**Description:** Internet installs can take 2+ weeks. Book now for your arrival date. Research providers at the new address first (check the address on each provider's site).

**Event:** Plan the drive route and book lodging
**Owner:** M | **Alert:** 10:00 AM
**Description:** Map dog-friendly stops every 2–3 hours. Book 2–3 nights of dog-friendly lodging along the route. Confirm pet fees. Save confirmation numbers in your documents folder.

**Event:** Get vehicle pre-move maintenance done
**Owner:** M | **Alert:** 9:00 AM
**Description:** Oil change, tire check, brakes, battery, fluids. Schedule the appointment this week if not already done. Oregon mountain passes are not forgiving on a neglected car.

---

## WEEK 6

**Event:** Start declutter — garage, storage, closets
**Owner:** J | **Alert:** 8:00 AM
**Description:** Anything you haven't used in a year is a candidate. Sell, donate, or trash. Schedule Facebook Marketplace pickups or a Goodwill run. Less stuff = cheaper move.

**Event:** Order packing supplies
**Owner:** P | **Alert:** 9:00 AM
**Description:** Boxes (small, medium, large, wardrobe), tape, bubble wrap, markers, mattress bags. Ask grocery and liquor stores for free boxes first. Order specialty boxes (TV, dish packs) online.

**Event:** Notify landlord in writing — Ohio move-out date
**Owner:** J | **Alert:** 8:00 AM
**Description:** Send written notice per lease terms. Request a move-out inspection and confirm deposit return process. Keep a copy of everything sent.

**Event:** Gather all important documents
**Owner:** J | **Alert:** 10:00 AM
**Description:** Collect licenses, passports, titles, Social Security cards, birth certificates, medical records, prescriptions, insurance policies, dog records. Put originals in one folder.

**Event:** Get auto insurance sorted for Oregon
**Owner:** M | **Alert:** 9:00 AM
**Description:** Call your current insurer. Confirm coverage during the move and update the policy to Oregon address upon arrival. Get the new insurance card before you leave Ohio.

---

## WEEK 5

**Event:** Begin packing — non-essential rooms
**Owner:** J | **Alert:** 8:00 AM
**Description:** Pack guest room, storage, seasonal items, decor, books, and anything you won't need for 5+ weeks. Label every box: room + contents + "FRAGILE" if needed. Pack a "Last Out, First In" box per room.

**Event:** Schedule Ohio utility shutoffs
**Owner:** J | **Alert:** 9:00 AM
**Description:** Electric, gas, water, trash — schedule final shutoff for the day after you leave. Take a photo of your account numbers. Keep them on until you're confirmed out.

**Event:** Set up Oregon utilities
**Owner:** M | **Alert:** 9:00 AM
**Description:** Contact electric, gas, and water providers at the Oregon address. Schedule start dates for move-in day. Confirm deposit requirements.

**Event:** Submit USPS change of address
**Owner:** J | **Alert:** 8:00 AM
**Description:** Go to usps.com and submit for both of you. Set the forwarding start date to your move date. It takes a few days to activate so don't wait longer than this.

**Event:** Notify bank, credit cards, and employer of address change
**Owner:** J | **Alert:** 10:00 AM
**Description:** Update with every financial institution, your employer's HR/payroll, and the Social Security Administration. Do this online or by phone. Keep a log of who you've notified.

---

## WEEK 4

**Event:** Pack kitchen — keep 1 week of essentials out
**Owner:** J | **Alert:** 8:00 AM
**Description:** Pack everything except one pot, one pan, plates and cutlery for the week, and coffee supplies. Donate or consume pantry items you won't move. Wrap dishes in packing paper; don't use newspaper.

**Event:** Pack living room and bedrooms (non-essentials)
**Owner:** J | **Alert:** 8:00 AM
**Description:** Books, decor, off-season clothes, extra bedding. Leave out what you need for the next 2 weeks. Label all boxes clearly with destination room in Oregon.

**Event:** Confirm mover appointment — final details
**Owner:** J | **Alert:** 9:00 AM
**Description:** Confirm arrival window, crew size, parking needs, and payment method. Ask about elevator reservations or parking permits if applicable at either address. Get the driver's cell number.

**Event:** Find a new vet in Oregon — make first appointment
**Owner:** M | **Alert:** 9:00 AM
**Description:** Research vets near the new address. Book a first visit for 1–2 weeks after arrival. Identify the nearest 24-hour emergency vet and save their number now.

**Event:** Cancel Ohio-specific subscriptions and services
**Owner:** J | **Alert:** 10:00 AM
**Description:** Gym memberships, local delivery services, Ohio-specific loyalty programs, newspaper subscriptions, pest control, lawn care. Update streaming and subscription addresses.

---

## WEEK 3

**Event:** Pack bathrooms — keep toiletry kit out
**Owner:** J | **Alert:** 8:00 AM
**Description:** Pack everything except a 1-week toiletry kit per person. Keep medications completely separate and accessible — never in the moving truck.

**Event:** Defrost and clean fridge — do this 48 hrs before mover arrival
**Owner:** J | **Alert:** 8:00 AM
**Description:** Use up or donate perishables this week. The fridge needs to be empty, dry, and defrosted before movers load it. Check your contract for requirements.

**Event:** Photograph all valuables and serial numbers
**Owner:** M | **Alert:** 9:00 AM
**Description:** Photo every valuable item, electronics serial numbers, and furniture condition. Email them to yourself and save to cloud storage. This protects you if anything is damaged or lost.

**Event:** Pack dog bag — keep it out and accessible
**Owner:** M | **Alert:** 9:00 AM
**Description:** Food (3+ day supply), water, bowls, leash, harness, meds, records, crate, favorite toy, blanket. This bag stays in the car, not the truck. Confirm the crate fits in the car.

**Event:** Confirm vehicle shipping pickup — if applicable
**Owner:** M | **Alert:** 9:00 AM
**Description:** Call the carrier. Confirm date, location, driver contact, and payment. Remove all personal items from the car being shipped — they're not covered. Take photos of the car's condition.

---

## WEEK 2

**Event:** Pack everything except moving day essentials
**Owner:** J | **Alert:** 8:00 AM
**Description:** Final push. Clothes for travel, toiletry kits, bedding for the last night, medications, dog bag, and documents folder stay out. Everything else goes in a box or bag.

**Event:** Confirm Oregon housing move-in details
**Owner:** J | **Alert:** 9:00 AM
**Description:** Confirm key pickup time, parking for the moving truck, and any move-in rules (elevator reservations, loading dock hours). Get the landlord's day-of number.

**Event:** Withdraw moving day cash
**Owner:** M | **Alert:** 10:00 AM
**Description:** $200–$300 for tips, tolls, and emergencies. Keep it separate from your wallet. Mover tips are $20–$50 per person for a job well done.

**Event:** Charge all devices and backup batteries
**Owner:** J | **Alert:** 8:00 PM (night before)
**Description:** Phones, laptops, tablets, portable battery packs. Pack car chargers and cables in the personal bag, not the moving truck.

---

## MOVE DAY — WEEK 0

**Event:** Moving day — start early
**Owner:** J | **Alert:** 6:00 AM
**Description:** Use the printed moving day essentials checklist in the glovebox. Walk through every room before you leave. Take a final video. Return keys and get a receipt. Don't sign a blank Bill of Lading.

**Event:** Dog settled and secure before movers arrive
**Owner:** M | **Alert:** 7:00 AM
**Description:** Set up the dog in one room with the door closed, or with a sitter, before movers start. Keep food, water, and the crate accessible. Move the dog to the car once loading begins.

---

## POST-MOVE — WEEK 1 IN OREGON

**Event:** Photograph new place at move-in
**Owner:** J | **Alert:** First morning
**Description:** Document every room, wall, floor, and appliance condition before unpacking. Send damage notes to landlord in writing within whatever deadline the lease specifies.

**Event:** Oregon DMV — get driver's license and register vehicle
**Owner:** M | **Alert:** Day 3–5
**Description:** Bring proof of residency, Ohio title, proof of insurance, and any other required docs. Check the Oregon DMV site for the current document checklist. Schedule an emissions test if you're in a required county.

**Event:** Update microchip registry — dog
**Owner:** M | **Alert:** Day 2
**Description:** Log into the microchip registry (check the brand: HomeAgain, PetLink, etc.) and update to your new address and phone number. Takes 5 minutes.

**Event:** Get Oregon dog license
**Owner:** M | **Alert:** Day 5–7
**Description:** Check your city or county requirements. Usually done online or at the county office. Bring proof of current rabies vaccination.

**Event:** Confirm all Ohio utility cancellations
**Owner:** J | **Alert:** Day 3
**Description:** Call or log in to confirm final bills and that accounts are closed. Keep the final statements for your records and for tax purposes.

**Event:** Update voter registration
**Owner:** J | **Alert:** Day 7
**Description:** Oregon auto-registers eligible residents through the DMV. Confirm your status at sos.oregon.gov after your license visit.

---

## A QUICK NOTE ON IMPORTING

If you're using **Google Calendar**, create a new calendar called "Move 2025" so these don't clutter your main calendar and you can hide or delete them all at once after the move. In **iCal / Apple Calendar**, same idea — create a dedicated calendar. Both let you set repeating alerts, so you can add a second nudge 2 days before anything that has a hard deadline.

turns.text:
# Packing Timeline & Room-by-Room Checklist

---

## THE LABELING SYSTEM

Simple and consistent beats elaborate. Use this across every box.

**Box Label Formula:**
```
DESTINATION ROOM — Contents (brief)
Priority: FIRST IN / NORMAL / LAST LOAD
Fragile: YES / NO
Owner: M / P / J
Box #: ___ of ___ (fill in total when the room is done)
```

**Color Code (use colored tape or markers):**
- 🔴 Red = Kitchen
- 🔵 Blue = Bedroom(s)
- 🟢 Green = Bathroom
- 🟡 Yellow = Living Room
- ⬜ White / Black = Office / Documents
- 🟠 Orange = Garage / Tools
- 🟣 Purple = Dog / Pet supplies
- ✳️ Star sticker = FIRST IN (unpack immediately)

---

## PRINTABLE BOX LABEL

Print or write on an index card and tape to the TOP and one SIDE of every box.

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  ROOM: _________________________________│
│  CONTENTS: _____________________________│
│  _______________________________________│
│  PRIORITY:  □ FIRST IN  □ NORMAL        │
│             □ LAST LOAD □ DO NOT LOAD * │
│  FRAGILE:   □ YES   □ NO               │
│  OWNER:     □ M   □ P   □ J            │
│  BOX #: _______ of _______ (this room) │
│  TOTAL WEIGHT (approx): _______________│
└─────────────────────────────────────────│
  * DO NOT LOAD = stays in the car
```

Tape one label to the **top** and one to a **side** so you can read it in a stack. Mark FRAGILE boxes on all four sides and the top.

---

## THE "LAST OUT / FIRST IN" BOX PLAN

Each room gets one dedicated box that is **packed last and loaded last** so it comes off the truck first. Mark it with a star sticker and "FIRST IN" on every side. These boxes ride together near the back of the truck door, not buried inside.

**What goes in a First In box — by room:**

**Kitchen First In Box** *(red star)*
One pot, one pan, one baking sheet, 2 sets of plates and cutlery, 2 mugs, dish soap, sponge, paper towels, coffee maker and coffee, can opener, and 2–3 days of non-perishable food.

**Bedroom First In Box** *(blue star)*
Bedding set for each bed (sheets, pillowcases, one blanket), pajamas, alarm clock or phone charger, eye masks if used, and any white noise machine.

**Bathroom First In Box** *(green star)*
Toilet paper (bring at least 4 rolls), hand soap, 2 towels per person, shower curtain and rings if yours, basic cleaning spray, and a small mirror.

**Office / Documents First In Box** *(white star)*
Power strip, laptop charger, router and cables, pens and notepad, any work items needed on day one.

**Living Room First In Box** *(yellow star)*
TV remote, any streaming device, one throw blanket, phone charger, and a lamp if overhead lighting is poor.

**Dog First In Box** *(purple star — stays in the car, not the truck)*
Food and bowls, water, leash, bed, familiar toy, poop bags, and a small treat bag.

**"Survival Kit" Bag — Rides in the Car**
This is not a box. It's a duffel or tote that never goes in the truck: 3–4 days of clothes per person, all medications, toiletry kits, phone chargers, documents folder, dog bag, cash, and snacks.

---

## PACKING SCHEDULE OVERVIEW

Your move is 10 weeks out. The goal is to have everything except daily essentials packed by **the end of Week 2 before move day** (8 weeks of packing across the schedule below).

| Week | Focus | Owner | Est. Time |
|---|---|---|---|
| 10–9 | Declutter whole house; order supplies | J | 4–8 hrs total |
| 8 | Storage, garage, off-season items | J | 4–6 hrs |
| 7 | Books, decor, guest room, spare closets | J | 3–5 hrs |
| 6 | Living room non-essentials, art, media | J | 2–4 hrs |
| 5 | Bedrooms (off-season clothes, extras) | J | 3–5 hrs |
| 4 | Kitchen (keep 1 week of essentials out) | J | 4–6 hrs |
| 3 | Bathrooms, office, remaining bedrooms | J | 3–4 hrs |
| 2 | Final sweep, First In boxes, essentials only remain | J | 2–3 hrs |
| 1 | Pack survival kit and dog bag. Done. | J | 1–2 hrs |

---

## DECLUTTER PRINCIPLES (do this before you pack anything)

The goal is simple: **don't pay to move things you don't want.** Moving costs scale with weight and volume, so every bag you donate is money saved.

Work through each room with three bins or areas: **Keep, Donate/Sell, and Trash.** A good rule of thumb is the 12-month rule — if you haven't used it in a year and it has no sentimental or practical value at the destination, let it go.

For selling: list on Facebook Marketplace, Craigslist, or OfferUp. Give yourself a deadline of 3 weeks before move day for pickups — after that, donate the rest. Don't let the perfect sale delay a donation run. Schedule a Goodwill or Salvation Army pickup online so it happens whether or not you get around to dropping things off.

For furniture: measure the new space before you move a single piece. If a couch doesn't fit the new living room, it's better to sell it in Ohio than to move it 2,400 miles and sell it in Oregon.

For sentimental items: keep them, but be intentional. One box of meaningful keepsakes is fine. Five boxes of "I might feel bad throwing this away" is a moving tax.

---

## ROOM-BY-ROOM PACKING CHECKLIST

---

### STORAGE UNIT / ATTIC / BASEMENT
**Owner: J | Estimated time: 4–6 hours | Timeline: Weeks 10–8**

This is your easiest win and your first priority. These spaces hold things you're already not using.

- [ ] **J** Sort everything into Keep, Donate, Trash before touching a single box *(2 hrs)*
- [ ] **J** Donate or sell holiday decorations you haven't used in 2+ years
- [ ] **J** Recycle or shred old documents you no longer need (keep 3–5 years of tax records)
- [ ] **J** Disassemble any furniture stored here and label hardware bags to the piece
- [ ] **J** Pack holiday decor and seasonal items you are keeping *(1–2 hrs)*
- [ ] **J** Pack sporting equipment, camping gear, and hobby items *(1 hr)*
- [ ] Label all boxes: STORAGE, contents, priority NORMAL unless you use them seasonally

**Declutter tip:** If you have duplicate tools, holiday decorations for a house size you're leaving, or exercise equipment with cobwebs on it, this is the moment. Shipping a treadmill cross-country costs more than buying a used one in Oregon.

---

### GARAGE
**Owner: J (M leads) | Estimated time: 4–6 hours | Timeline: Weeks 9–8**

- [ ] **M** Sort tools: keep what you use, donate or sell duplicates *(1 hr)*
- [ ] **M** Properly dispose of hazardous materials — paint, motor oil, pesticides, propane tanks. Movers will not transport these and you legally cannot pack them in a rental truck. Check your city's hazardous waste drop-off schedule. *(1 hr to sort and schedule)*
- [ ] **M** Drain and clean the lawn mower and any gas-powered equipment before packing
- [ ] **J** Decide what large equipment is worth moving vs. selling (lawn mower, snowblower, patio furniture). Oregon has different needs than Ohio.
- [ ] **M** Pack hand tools in toolboxes; wrap power tools in moving blankets or bubble wrap *(1–2 hrs)*
- [ ] **M** Pack garage shelving contents into clearly labeled boxes *(1 hr)*
- [ ] **J** Disassemble shelving units and label hardware
- [ ] **J** Measure large items (patio furniture, bikes) against the new space before packing

**Declutter tip:** Snowblowers, heavy-duty ice scrapers, and Ohio-specific winter gear may not be worth the cost to ship to Portland or Bend. Patio furniture is bulky and cheap to replace. Bikes are worth moving. Tools are worth moving unless duplicated.

**Hazardous items to dispose of, NOT pack:**
Paint and stain, motor oil, gasoline, propane tanks (even "empty"), pesticides and herbicides, pool chemicals, batteries (car batteries), and aerosol cans. Search "[your city] hazardous waste disposal" for drop-off locations.

---

### GUEST ROOM / SPARE ROOM
**Owner: J | Estimated time: 2–3 hours | Timeline: Week 8–7**

- [ ] **J** Strip and donate any bedding you're replacing
- [ ] **J** Declutter the closet — this is often where things go to be forgotten
- [ ] **J** Pack extra linens and bedding into vacuum compression bags (saves 60–70% of space)
- [ ] **J** Pack decor, lamps, and wall art
- [ ] **J** Disassemble bed frame; bag and label hardware, tape the bag to the headboard
- [ ] **J** Pack dresser contents in drawers or into boxes; tape drawers shut for the move if the dresser is staying assembled
- [ ] **J** Pack closet contents into wardrobe boxes or garbage bags (clothes on hangers can go directly into a wardrobe box in 5 minutes)

---

### LIVING ROOM
**Owner: J | Estimated time: 3–4 hours | Timeline: Weeks 7–6**

- [ ] **J** Declutter books — donate what you won't reread. Books are extremely heavy and expensive to move. *(30 min)*
- [ ] **J** Pack books into small boxes only (a large box of books will break or be unmovable)
- [ ] **J** Wrap and pack decorative items, picture frames, and sculptures *(1 hr)*
- [ ] **J** Remove and roll area rugs; wrap in plastic stretch wrap or old sheets
- [ ] **J** Pack media: DVDs, vinyl, games *(30 min)*
- [ ] **J** Wrap TV in moving blankets or original box if kept; label the TV box FRAGILE on all sides
- [ ] **J** Disassemble entertainment center and label all hardware
- [ ] **J** Take down and wrap all wall art and mirrors (mirrors get a dedicated mirror box or cardboard sandwich — don't wrap them in a standard box)
- [ ] **J** Pack throw pillows and blankets into vacuum compression bags
- [ ] **J** Leave out: one lamp, one throw, remote, phone charger until moving week

**Declutter tip:** Oversized furniture that won't fit the new space should be sold now, not moved and then sold. Measure your new living room and compare it to what you have before packing a single piece.

---

### HOME OFFICE
**Owner: M | Estimated time: 2–3 hours | Timeline: Week 6–5**

- [ ] **M** Shred and recycle old documents (keep tax records, legal docs, medical records)
- [ ] **M** Back up computer files to an external drive and cloud storage before packing
- [ ] **M** Photograph cable setups before unplugging everything
- [ ] **M** Label every cable with masking tape and a marker before coiling and packing
- [ ] **M** Pack monitors with original boxes if kept, or use mirror/picture boxes with padding
- [ ] **M** Pack desk accessories, office supplies, and books into small and medium boxes
- [ ] **M** Disassemble desk; label hardware
- [ ] **M** Keep in car: laptop, chargers, external drive, documents folder, any work-critical items

---

### BEDROOMS (PRIMARY AND SECONDARY)
**Owner: J | Estimated time: 3–5 hours total | Timeline: Weeks 6–4**

**Week 6–5 (non-essentials):**
- [ ] **J** Donate or sell clothing you haven't worn in a year — do this before packing anything
- [ ] **J** Pack off-season clothing into vacuum compression bags or medium boxes *(1 hr)*
- [ ] **J** Pack extra shoes (keep one or two pairs out per person)
- [ ] **J** Pack books, decor, extra bedding

**Week 4–3 (the rest):**
- [ ] **J** Pack remaining clothing into wardrobe boxes or suitcases (use your suitcases as boxes — they're going anyway)
- [ ] **J** Pack nightstand contents; leave out what you use nightly
- [ ] **J** Disassemble bed frame; bag and label hardware
- [ ] **J** Wrap and pack lamps (shades in separate boxes, lightly stuffed with tissue)
- [ ] **J** Pack dresser contents; tape drawers or remove and pack contents separately
- [ ] **J** Pack jewelry and valuables in a bag that rides in the car, not the truck
- [ ] **J** Leave out: one set of bedding, one pillow per person, phone charger, alarm, 3–4 days of clothes

**Declutter tip:** Suitcases, duffel bags, and laundry baskets all make excellent boxes. Fill them with soft items like clothing, linens, and stuffed animals. It costs nothing and reduces the number of boxes you need.

---

### KITCHEN
**Owner: J | Estimated time: 4–6 hours | Timeline: Week 5–4**

The kitchen is the most time-consuming room and the one most people underestimate. Start earlier than you think you need to.

**Week 5 — Declutter and start:**
- [ ] **J** Go through every cabinet. Donate duplicate gadgets, appliances you never use, chipped dishes, and expired pantry items. *(1–2 hrs)*
- [ ] **J** Decide which pantry staples you'll use up vs. donate vs. move. Plan meals around what's left.
- [ ] **J** Decide on large appliances: stand mixer, air fryer, instant pot. Each is heavy. Only keep what you genuinely use monthly.

**Week 4 — Pack almost everything:**
- [ ] **J** Pack small appliances (wrap cords around the appliance and tape them, or bag them separately) *(1 hr)*
- [ ] **J** Pack dishes: wrap each plate individually in packing paper, stack vertically (not flat — they break flat), into dish pack boxes *(1–2 hrs)*
- [ ] **J** Pack glasses and mugs: each one in paper, stuffed with paper inside, into dish boxes
- [ ] **J** Pack pots and pans: nest them with paper between each layer
- [ ] **J** Pack pantry items in small boxes (canned goods are very heavy — keep boxes under 30 lbs)
- [ ] **J** Pack spices in a zip-lock bag inside a box; they spill everywhere
- [ ] **J** Pack sharp knives wrapped in paper and taped, or in a knife block, labeled SHARP
- [ ] **J** Label all kitchen boxes FRAGILE on the sides and top

**Leave out until moving week:**
One pot, one pan, one baking sheet, 2 plates and sets of cutlery, 2 mugs, coffee maker, dish soap, sponge, and can opener. These become your First In box.

**Declutter tip:** A cross-country move is a natural kitchen reset. Duplicate pans, gadgets used twice a year, mismatched plastic containers without lids, water bottles you have 11 of — now is the time. The dollar-per-pound cost to ship cast iron or a full set of dishes is real. Keep what you love

# 2) FINAL 14-DAY PACKING CHECKLIST
### Day 0 = Move Day. Count back from your date.

**Key:** Each day has a primary owner, a focus area, and an estimated active working time. "Active time" means hands-on packing, not the whole day.

---

**DAY 14 | Owner: J | Est. time: 2–3 hrs**
Whole-house sweep and supply check. Walk every room and make a written list of what still needs packing. Confirm you have enough boxes, tape, bubble wrap, and markers. Order or buy anything missing today — don't wait. Identify any large items (furniture, rugs, mirrors) that need special materials and get those too. This is a planning day, not a packing day.

---

**DAY 13 | Owner: M | Est. time: 3–4 hrs**
Office and electronics. Back up the computer to cloud and an external drive before unplugging anything. Photograph all cable setups. Label every cable before coiling. Pack monitors, printers, and desk accessories. Disassemble the desk and bag hardware. Leave out: laptop, one charger, external drive. These ride in the car.

---

**DAY 12 | Owner: P | Est. time: 3–4 hrs**
Guest room and spare closets. Strip the guest bed, pack linens into compression bags, disassemble the frame and bag hardware. Clear and pack the spare closet completely — this is usually the last holdout of random unsorted items, so leave extra time for decision-making. Donate anything that surfaces here rather than packing it.

---

**DAY 11 | Owner: J | Est. time: 3–4 hrs**
Living room. Pack all remaining books (small boxes only — heavy), wall art, mirrors, and decor. Roll and wrap area rugs. Pack media. Wrap and box the TV if not already done. Leave out: one lamp, one throw blanket, remote, phone charger.

---

**DAY 10 | Owner: J | Est. time: 4–5 hrs**
Kitchen — the big one. Pack all small appliances, pantry items (small boxes for canned goods), spices (sealed in zip-lock bags), and serveware. Wrap and box all dishes and glasses individually. Pack pots and pans with paper between each. Label every box FRAGILE. Leave out: one pot, one pan, 2 plates and sets of cutlery, 2 mugs, coffee maker, dish soap, sponge, can opener.

---

**DAY 9 | Owner: J | Est. time: 2–3 hrs**
Kitchen overflow and fridge prep. Finish any remaining kitchen packing. Use up, donate, or discard remaining perishables. Begin running down the fridge. Do a full declutter pass on the pantry — moving canned goods 2,400 miles rarely makes sense. If you have a chest freezer, start running it down now.

---

**DAY 8 | Owner: J | Est. time: 3–4 hrs**
Primary bedroom non-essentials. Pack off-season and extra clothing into compression bags or suitcases. Pack shoes (keep 2 pairs per person out). Pack jewelry and valuables into a bag that will ride in the car. Pack extra bedding. Leave out: 3–4 days of clothes per person, one pillow each, phone chargers.

---

**DAY 7 | Owner: J | Est. time: 2–3 hrs**
Midpoint check and buffer day. Do a room-by-room walk with your box list. Number all packed boxes and log them (a simple spreadsheet or notes app works). Confirm the mover's arrival time and parking plan. If anything is behind, use today to catch up. If you're on track, start building the First In boxes so they're ready to go.

---

**DAY 6 | Owner: J | Est. time: 3–4 hrs**
Bathrooms and linen closet. Pack everything except a 3-day toiletry kit per person. Pack towels (great box fillers around fragile items), extra toilet paper, and cleaning supplies. Leave out: toilet paper (at least 4 rolls), hand soap, 2 towels per person, toothbrushes and toothpaste, any daily medications. Medications never go in the truck.

---

**DAY 5 | Owner: M | Est. time: 2–3 hrs**
Dog bag and pet supplies. Pack everything for the dog that isn't needed daily: extra food, backup leash, carrier or crate (if it fits in the car), grooming supplies. Build the dog's First In box: food and bowls, water, leash, bed, familiar toy, poop bags, records. Set this aside and label it DO NOT LOAD — it goes in the car.

---

**DAY 4 | Owner: J | Est. time: 3–4 hrs**
Final bedroom sweep and garage stragglers. Pack the last remaining bedroom items — nightstand contents, lamps, remaining decor. Finish anything left in the garage. Confirm all hazardous materials have been disposed of. Disassemble any remaining furniture and bag all hardware. Take photos of assembled furniture before disassembly if it helps with reassembly.

---

**DAY 3 | Owner: J | Est. time: 2–3 hrs**
Build all First In boxes. One per room: kitchen, bedroom(s), bathroom, office, living room. Seal and star-label them. Stack them together near the door so they load last and come off the truck first. Fridge should be fully emptied and defrosting by end of day. Do a full walk-through of every room, cabinet, closet, shelf, and drawer. If it's not in a box or labeled as staying out, it should be.

---

**DAY 2 | Owner: J | Est. time: 1–2 hrs**
Survival kit and final loose ends. Pack the car survival bag: 3–4 days of clothes per person, all medications, toiletry kits, phone chargers, documents folder, dog bag, snacks, water, cash. Confirm it all fits in the car with the dog and the dog's crate. Charge all devices and battery packs overnight. Confirm the mover's arrival window one more time by phone.

---

**DAY 1 (Eve of Move Day) | Owner: J | Est. time: 1 hr**
Nothing should need packing today. Wipe down the fridge interior once fully defrosted and dry. Take a final photo walk-through of the whole home while it still has your stuff in it. Lay out the moving day essentials checklist (the one-pager) on the kitchen counter. Set an early alarm. Sleep.

---

**DAY 0 — MOVE DAY | Owner: J**
Use the printed moving day essentials checklist. Everything else is done.

---
